title: Spline Policy: A Structured Representation for Robot Policies
key_concept: Action chunks are flat arrays: no notion of smoothness, no temporal structure, no way to constrain or edit pre-execution. You're discretizing a continuous motion into a fixed grid and hoping the policy compensates. That's geometric information thrown away by design.

title: Difference-Aware Retrieval Policies for Imitation Learning
key_concept: Behavior cloning learns state→action globally. But at test time, small errors compound — you drift off-distribution and the policy has no anchor. The model memorized a global map but gets lost the moment it steps off the training path.

title: When to Align, When to Predict: A Phase Diagram for Multimodal Learning
key_concept: CLIP-style alignment (CA) and cross-modal prediction (CP) are the two dominant paradigms. But practitioners in biomedicine or astrophysics keep finding their best single modality beats both. Nobody had a principled explanation — until now.

title: Anatomy of Post-Training: Using Interpretability to Characterize Data and Shape the Learning Signal
key_concept: RLHF collapses rich behavioral signals into a scalar reward. That compression destroys provenance — you can't tell if a model learned "be helpful" or "be verbose and confident." Spurious correlations get baked in silently. The loss function has no concept of concepts.

title: Learning to Reason by Analogy via Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
key_concept: Standard RAG ranks by embedding cosine similarity. But two problems can be semantically distant yet share the same underlying algebraic structure. You need a retriever that asks: "does this example teach the right *move*?" — not "does this example *look* similar?"

title: LabVLA: Grounding Vision-Language-Action Models in Scientific Laboratories
key_concept: VLA models trained on household demos fail in labs. Transparent liquid physics, fixed instrument layouts, strict protocol ordering — none of that appears in standard robot datasets. It's a distribution mismatch that accuracy metrics don't even capture cleanly.

title: World Tracing: Generative Pixel-Aligned Geometry Beyond the Visible
key_concept: The core tension: depth predictors are anchored (faithful) but surface-only. Image-to-3D models are complete but geometrically unmoored. You can't have both... unless you reframe geometry as an *ordered sequence of ray intersections* per pixel, not just the first hit.

title: Gaze Heads: How VLMs Look at What They Describe
key_concept: The core problem: we had no idea *how* a VLM decides what to describe when. Is it diffuse across all heads? Learned implicitly? Turns out it's localized — a tiny circuit, findable via correlation scores over a handful of forward passes using comic strips as spatial ground truth.

title: Hierarchical Advantage Weighting for Online RL Fine-Tuning of VLAs from Sparse Episode Outcomes
key_concept: The core problem: one binary reward conflates two things — did the policy *survive* (viability) and did it *move fast* (efficiency)? Once you're succeeding, the gradient goes silent. You can't improve speed from a signal that just says "yes."

title: Explaining Attention with Program Synthesis
key_concept: Attention heads are black boxes: we know *what* they output, not *why*. The goal is symbolic explanations — rules a human can read and verify. The gap between "this head attends to previous nouns" and a formal, testable program has always been the hard part.

title: Actionable Activation Directions for Detecting and Mitigating Emergent Misalignment Across Language Model Families
key_concept: Fine-tuning on insecure code induces "emergent misalignment" — models start behaving badly *beyond* code tasks. The question: is this a geometric structure in activation space, or just diffuse noise? Difference-in-means gives a clean answer: it's a direction.

title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
key_concept: Autoregressive models have natural checkpoints: each token is a readable state. Diffusion models smear computation across denoising steps with no such bottleneck. Measuring interpretability requires knowing *where* meaning lives — and diffusion models hide that.

title: LedgerAgent: Structured State for Policy-Adherent Tool-Calling Agents
key_concept: Standard agents dump everything — observations, tool returns, policies — into one flat prompt. The model must re-derive what's true *now* from what was true *then*. That's not memory. That's archaeology. Stale facts slip through undetected.

title: The Token Is a Group Element: On Lie-Algebra Attention over Matrix Lie Groups
key_concept: Standard geometric attention encodes poses as feature vectors, then fights to bake in equivariance via irreps or spherical harmonics. But those tools break for non-compact groups like affine transforms with scale and shear. You're designing around a gap in the theory.

title: Open Problem: Is AdamW Effective Under Heavy-Tailed Noise?
key_concept: Gradient noise in LLM pretraining is heavy-tailed — infinite variance, fat tails, occasional catastrophic spikes. Most AdamW theory assumes finite variance. That's like designing a bridge for average loads while ignoring that trucks exist.

title: Posterior Refinement: Fast Language Generation via Any-Order Flow Maps
key_concept: Non-autoregressive models can generate all tokens in parallel, but they break independence assumptions. MDMs fix this iteratively but suffer factorization error — each token is scored in isolation, so joint consistency collapses when you unmask many tokens at once.
